concept.title: Journey departure-table attendant
concept.scene: At a covered canal departure pavilion before sunrise, a fictional attendant operates a counterweight-driven route table whose gear-linked brass boat marker advances between engraved stations; an arriving passenger boat supplies the visible practical context.

ownership: All six scene relations are agent-owned experimental observations fixed before retrieval. They do not become requester-owned anchors, source assertions or future authorial locks. Appearance-reference criterion follows the chosen face/hair use scope.
judgment_policy: Review actual saved pixels. For each multi-component relation every owner, part, connection and distinguishing state must be visible together. partial or unobservable cannot pass. Rendered stills can support structural depiction, not physical engineering performance or real motion. User acceptance remains pending.

observable_relations.relation: Iron weight -> taut cord wound around drive drum
observable_relations.pass_criteria: The same suspended iron weight, continuous cord and cord-to-drum winding are visible together, with the weight free below its support.
observable_relations.baseline_evidence: A pear-shaped iron weight hangs freely beneath a cord wound around an exposed drive drum

observable_relations.relation: Drive drum shaft -> toothed wheel -> meshing second wheel and terminal pinion
observable_relations.pass_criteria: A traceable shaft/wheel connection and actual visible touching gear teeth connect the drum to the downstream pinion. Loose decorative gears fail the full relation.
observable_relations.baseline_evidence: The drum shaft carries a toothed wheel meshing with a second wheel and a smaller terminal pinion

observable_relations.relation: Terminal pinion -> toothed rack -> boat-marker carriage beneath route line
observable_relations.pass_criteria: Pinion teeth visibly engage the rack, and the same rack structurally carries the marker carriage on the route board. Merely nearby marker and gears are partial.
observable_relations.baseline_evidence: The terminal pinion engages a horizontal toothed rack fixed to the boat-marker carriage, which runs directly beneath the engraved route line

observable_relations.relation: Escapement wheel -> contacting pallet -> lever -> pendulum
observable_relations.pass_criteria: Wheel/pallet contact and a lever link to the pendulum can be followed within the same open frame. A clock face or hanging pendulum alone is insufficient.
observable_relations.baseline_evidence: An escapement wheel contacts a pallet on a lever visibly linked to a slender pendulum

observable_relations.relation: Attendant -> removed key at lowered right hand; opposite palm -> outer frame
observable_relations.pass_criteria: The hands belong to the same subject, key is visibly held clear of the machine at her hip, the opposite palm rests on the outer frame, and the arms leave the drive structure readable.
observable_relations.baseline_evidence: holding it loosely in her lowered right hand beside her hip, while her left palm rests on the outer oak frame

observable_relations.relation: Departure-table foreground -> pavilion opening -> actual arriving canal boat
observable_relations.pass_criteria: The table and subject occupy a coherent departure pavilion with an identifiable real boat at the landing through its opening; the brass marker remains a separate smaller table component.
observable_relations.baseline_evidence: with the approaching boat readable between the stone columns behind them

appearance_reference_criterion.pass_criteria: The generated face is visibly guided by the supplied portrait in its softly tapered proportions, dark eyes and natural lip form, with a short dark bob and fine separated fringe. Assess visible guidance without asserting actual identity, biography, age or perfect likeness. If the face or hair is too small or obscured, record partial or unobservable.
